note: TOWN_LIFE §3.1 (TL-A2): a dawn sweeper with a broom (the crowd hangs the broom on the right hand: socket): two strokes from the right side across to the left, the second a little shorter, bent forward over the broom; a 2 s loop. Legs are ABSOLUTE on a STAND1 base (slightly bent, the same on every key: the feet never slide). Arms REACH: the right (lower) wrist is solved every frame to a point from the pelvis's head ([forward, up, right] metres); the left (top) wrist goes 0.3 m up the handle, on the line from the broom's floor point ([forward, right] from the pelvis's ground projection) through the right hand; the right wrist rolls so the broom (socket) stays along the handle. lean = spine forward, head = nod forward (looks at the floor), twist = + turns the chest left (follows the stroke). Shared by both skeletons.
